subject: Re: Model shortlist, context bands, and ramp milestones for FinBridge onboarding
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@finbridge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps after demo — model & context needs

Jonas, thanks again for the demo this morning — the FinBridge product team is excited. Quick follow-up so we can start internal procurement and scheduling:

- We expect two primary usage patterns: customer support chat (long threads, occasional attachments) and account-summary generation (shorter prompts, many calls).
- For planning, we think ~120k monthly active end users, with an initial pilot of ~10k MAU for 30 days.
- Typical per-interaction sizes (rough estimate): prompt ~300–400 tokens, model reply ~180–300 tokens. Some support threads require up to 20–25k of context for full history/attachments parsing.

Can you propose a concise shortlist (2–3 model tiers), recommended context bands (8k vs 32k), and a first-pass monthly token estimate and an expected peak tokens/sec for the pilot? Also include any guidance on suggested reserved capacity vs hosted autoscale for the pilot.

We're aiming to lock procurement requirements by EOD next Wednesday so procurement can start the PO.

— Alex
Product Lead, FinBridge
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@finbridge.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finbridge.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps after demo — model & context needs

Alex — thanks, great summary. Below is a pragmatic shortlist and an initial sizing pass for the pilot + production ramp. I kept estimations conservative where context needs differ. Attached: finbridge_model_shortlist_v1.xlsx and token_traffic_estimates.csv.

Model shortlist (2-tier recommendation):
- Tier A (accuracy / long-context): Redwood-70B-32k (quantized GGUF q4_0) — best for support threads that need full context. Expected higher cost but lower failure modes for hallucinations when long history matters.
- Tier B (cost-efficient): Redwood-13B-q4_0-8k or Mistral-instruct-7B-8k — lower unit cost, good for account-summary generation and short chats.
- Fallback: Redwood-13B-8k warmed/cached for most bursts; route support threads to 70B when memory footprint indicates long history.

Context bands recommendation:
- Default: 8k for ~85% of calls (summaries, short chats).
- Long-context route (32k): for support ticket threads and attachment parsing (~15% initial). Implement routing rule based on message-length heuristics and an explicit "long context" flag from FinBridge UI.

Token volume (pilot = 10k MAU; full = 120k MAU):
- Pilot (10k MAU, 30 days): assume 1.8 interactions/user/day average -> 18k sessions/day. Avg tokens/session = prompt 350 + reply 220 = 570 tokens.
  - Daily tokens (pilot): 18,000 * 570 = ~10.26M tokens/day -> ~308M tokens/month (30d).
  - Monthly pilot tokens (30-day pilot): ~308M tokens.
- Full (120k MAU steady-state, conservative): 1.8 interactions/user/day -> 216k sessions/day -> 216,000 * 570 = ~123.1M tokens/day -> ~3.7B tokens/month.

Peak sizing (observed spikes):
- Baseline QPS (pilot): 18k sessions/day -> average ~0.21 req/sec; expect peaks up to 30 req/sec during business hours.
- Token/sec peak estimate: assume peak 30 req/sec * avg 570 tokens/session = ~17,100 tokens/sec. Add headroom x1.5 -> plan for ~26k tokens/sec peak for pilot.

Serving recommendations:
- Pilot: Hosted autoscale with conservative concurrency limits; enable prefix caching for reused contexts. Use quantized 13B as default. For long-context support routes, warm 70B nodes on-demand but consider a small dedicated pool if long-context usage rises >20% of traffic.
- Production ramp (120k MAU): move to Dedicated (reserved) capacity for Tier B baseline and a small reserved pool for Tier A (32k) or set up cross-region fallback.

Operational notes / risks:
- 32k context increases memory / GPU footprint significantly — expect 3–4x cost per request vs 8k for same model.
- Attachment parsing: prefer transcode->text before passing to model to reduce tokens. If you need native attachment context on model side, factor in additional tokens per attachment (~1k–6k depending on size).

Next steps I need from you by EOD Wed:
1) Confirm pilot MAU target (10k) and expected pilot start date.
2) Which workflows must have 32k context from day 1 (list IDs).
3) FinBridge SOW contact & purchase process so I can loop in contracts.

I'll loop in Solutions (Grace) and Implementation (Monica) on a sizing call tomorrow to lock the mutual action plan.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Moreno <alex@finbridge.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finbridge.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Next steps after demo — implementation sizing notes

Forwarding a quick implementation view from SRE/Implementation:

Jonas / Monica — from an implementation perspective here are pragmatic recommendations to turn the above into an ops-ready plan:

1) Pilot capacity plan (30-day):
   - Baseline: Hosted–Autoscale nodes serving Tier B (13B-q4) with burstable reserved option. Estimate equivalent of 2 x A100-40GB nodes warm to support concurrent bursts with batching (batch size ~4).
   - Long-context (32k): Use on-demand H100-backed instances or shared dedicated pool. For the pilot, a small warm pool of 1 H100-equivalent GPU (or 2x A100-80GB) should handle routing for the ~15% long-context volume with acceptable latency.

2) Quantization & runtime:
   - Use q4_0 GGUF for 13B to get 3–4x throughput improvements and lower memory. For 70B 32k, use custom kernel selection + 4-bit quantization; expect request latency 2.5–3x of 13B for comparable sequence lengths.

3) Caching & batching policy:
   - Enable prefix/KV caching for known templates (account summaries). Set batching target 40–80ms latency window for best throughput/latency tradeoff.

4) Observability & regression checks:
   - Add a small eval set for key prompts (support & summaries). Wire Redwood Optimize to monitor quality regressions correlated with quantization or model swaps.

5) Implementation kickoff: propose tomorrow 10:00 PT for a 60-min sizing + MAP sync. Monica, can you confirm resource owners for infra & data access (S3 bucket or API)?

— Grace
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@finbridge.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finbridge.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Next steps after demo — model & context needs (MAP + kickoff)

Alex / Priya — thanks both. Summary and agreed immediate actions below so procurement can proceed. I attached the mutual_action_plan.pdf to this thread.

Summary decisions:
- Pilot scope: 10k MAU, start window target 14 Jul 2025.
- Model routing: Default -> 13B q4_0 (8k); Long-context route -> 70B quantized (32k) for support only.
- Pilot token estimate (30d): ~308M tokens. Production steady-state estimate (120k MAU): ~3.7B tokens/month (used for budgeting).

Action items:
1) FinBridge (Alex): Confirm pilot start date (target 14 Jul) and list of workflows requiring 32k by 2025-07-02.
2) FinBridge (Procurement): Send PO contact + procurement timeline; we'll provide a 30-day pilot billing estimate and a draft PO statement once we have confirmed start date.
3) Redwood (Monica): Prepare implementation runbook and S3/access checklist by 2025-07-01.
4) Redwood (Grace): Join kickoff meeting to review capacity playbook and DB access for attachment parsing.
5) Redwood (Rishi): Prepare a quick-cost model (expected $/1M tokens) for both tiers and two toggle scenarios (with/without 32k usage) and share in the MAP doc.

Kickoff: 14 Jul 2025, 10:00 PT (60 min) — provisional calendar invite sent.

If that works I'll mark the MAP as agreed and Monica will begin provisioning. Thanks — looking forward.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
